messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: In the Mounjaro prescribing information, SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834) was a 40-week trial.
The trial was in adults with type 2 diabetes.
The adults had blood sugar that was not adequately controlled with diet and exercise alone.
Patients received once-weekly Mounjaro 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg, or placebo.
After 40 weeks, 78% to 85% of adults taking Mounjaro achieved an HbA1c below 7%.
This is compared with 23% of adults taking a placebo.
The average HbA1c change was -1.8% with Mounjaro 5 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 10 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 15 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -0.1% with placebo.
Triplet: ["SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834)", "participant population", "adults with type 2 diabetes"]

The relation 'participant population' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject clinical trial included participants from the specified population group.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has participant': The subject study or trial includes the entity specified by the object as a participant or group.
B. 'used in population': The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
C. 'has clinical trial result': The subject drug has demonstrated or shown the clinical trial outcome specified by the object entity.
D. 'has side effect more likely in': The subject drug is more likely to cause the specified adverse effect or reaction in the population or group specified by the object entity.
E. 'compared with': The subject drug was compared to the other drug or substance in a study.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
